text:
sam: Pushed a quick perf dump from a failing TP run — seeing big all-reduce tail on small-fragment workloads. flame link: https://perf.internal/redwood/2129991234
marco: saw that. what's the fraction of <16KB reduces? small frags usually kill ring perf.
sam: ~58% of reduces in that trace are <12KB,avg latency per reduce ~420us vs 110us for larger ones. attached pprof + NCCL traces in the bucket.
perf-bot: aggregate stats for run 2129991234:
  - total tokens: 4.2M
  - reduces: 312k (small=<12KB: 58%)
  - mean reduce latency: 235us
  - p50 end-to-end step: 26ms
  - p95 end-to-end step: 74ms

hao: this looks like KV-cache fragmentation + kernel selection mismatch. when KV cache warms we emit a lot of short KV pushes for newly requested prefixes -> small message all-reduces. ring gets terrible startup latency for many tiny msgs.
jess: agreed. tree algorithm handles small msgs better in our NCCL build because it reduces hop-count for tiny payloads. can we autoswitch in kernel selector based on msg size distribution?
marco: we already have a soft-fallback in the selector, but threshold is very conservative. forcing tree for <16KB in local test gave 9-12% step latency improvement for TP-8.
sam: can you share the command you used to force tree? I'll kick a staging run.
marco: sure: `export REDWOOD_NCCL_REDUCE_ALGO=tree && ./run_tp_inference --profile --trace=nvlink` — also changed selector to `msgsize_switch=16384` on the node-agent to force it.
hao: another angle — KV cache coalescing heuristics. right now we flush per-segment which fragments reductions. propose a tiny buffering window (3-5ms) or accumulate by destination rank to coalesce small KV updates before sending. that will reduce small-message pressure without switching algorithms.
jess: buffering sounds safe if we ensure it doesn't increase tail for real low-latency requests. maybe only apply when backlog>X or when predicted compute won't stall.
sam: can we run two parallel experiments on staging: (A) force tree at 16KB; (B) enable coalescing window=4ms + rank-accumulate. measure p95 and cost tokens.
marco: running A now on staging-8gpu, key: `staging-8g-tp-tree-16k`. I'll post results in ~20m.
perf-bot: experiment A started at 2129991300. baseline (previous run id 2129989000) -> p95 74ms baseline.
marco: A finished: p95 -> 66ms (11% improvement), mean reduce latency for small msgs -> 210us (was 420us). cost delta negligible.
hao: nice. B queued; small note — B requires a patch to runtime's kv-flusher, branch `kv/coalesce-4ms`.
sam: @hao do you want help with rollout? I can attach a canary route in dedicated to run B on a subset of traffic.
hao: thanks. will ping when branch ready.
marco: minor gotcha: when forcing tree we saw a slight CPU increase on host for scatter/gather. negligible on our nodes but flag it in release notes.
jess: follow ups: 1) add dynamic msgsize threshold in kernel selector using moving-window histogram; 2) metric for "small-reduce-rate" in console; 3) add kv-coalesce opt behind feature flag.
sam: sounds good. PRs: marco -> selector autoswitch + flag, hao -> kv coalesce branch. I'll own staging run orchestration and perf dashboard annotations.
perf-bot: note recorded: 2129991400: plan -> autoswitch + kv-coalesce feature-flag rollout. Assigned: marco, hao, sam.

sam: thanks team — good win. we'll validate A/B for a day then ramp.
